LESSON: METALLIC MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.2: Metallic materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Metallic materials, part of Materials for Production in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are metallic materials used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Metallic materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: the learner develops interacting skills when downloading and watching a video clip simulating physical

properties of metallic materials.

• Communication and collaboration: the learner acquires speaking, listening, and teamwork skills during discussion and

sharing of their findings with peers on the various uses of metallic materials in the locality.

Values:
• Unity: learner displays team spirit and collaboration with others during discussion and sharing of their findings with peers

on the various uses of metallic materials in the locality.

• Responsibility: learner shows accountability by completion of a chart to match metallic materials to their use in the work

environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education and mentorship: the learner develops inter-personal relationships while sharing findings with peers on various

uses of metallic materials in the locality.

Link to Other Subjects:

Integrated Science as learners learn about the periodic table in classification of metals
